faq.q: What was the Pan-African Congress of 1945?
faq.a: A meeting in Manchester, England, in October 1945, attended by future leaders like Kwame Nkrumah and Jomo Kenyatta. It demanded independence for African colonies.

The leader of Ghana's independence movement and its first prime minister, later president. Ghana, formerly the Gold Coast, became independent on 6 March 1957, often called the first sub-Saharan colony to do so.

faq.q: What was the Year of Africa?
faq.a: 1960, when 17 African countries became independent, including Nigeria, Senegal, Madagascar, Somalia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
asks: Why is 1960 called the Year of Africa?

faq.q: What was the Organisation of African Unity?
faq.a: An organisation of independent African states founded in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in 1963 to support freedom and cooperation. It was replaced by the African Union in 2002.

faq.q: Which was the last African colony to become independent?
faq.a: Namibia, ruled by South Africa, became independent in 1990, often seen as the end of colonial rule in mainland Africa. South Sudan became Africa's newest country in 2011, after splitting from Sudan.

facts: Seventeen African countries became independent in 1960.
The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity in 2002.
